title: Dornan's Spur Bar
venue_description:
Historic Family Establishment in Grand Teton National Park

Dornan's is a privately-owned family establishment located within the boundaries of Grand Teton National Park in Moose Wyoming. Originally homesteaded in 1922 by Evelyn Dornan the property has remained in the family for over a century and is now operated by the fifth generation of Dornans. The venue sits along the Snake River offering spectacular views of the Teton Range making it one of the most scenic locations in Jackson Hole.

The Jackson Hole Hootenanny

Dornan's is best known as the summer home of the Jackson Hole Hootenanny an acoustic open mic night that has been a valley tradition since the 1950s. What began as informal jam sessions under the Snake River bridge led by legendary mountaineer and skier Bill Briggs evolved into a formal event that moved to Dornan's in the early 1990s. The Hootenanny takes place every Monday evening with sign-ups beginning at 5:00 PM and performances running from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM. During summer months the event happens outdoors at the Chuckwagon stage while winter sessions relocate to the Silver Dollar Bar at the Wort Hotel in downtown Jackson.

Musical Heritage

The Hootenanny has launched the careers of several notable musicians and has become a rite of passage for Jackson Hole's music community. Legendary performers like John Denver and Chuck Pyle made surprise appearances at the venue. The event maintains a strict acoustic-only policy with performers limited to two songs per set though repeats are welcome if time allows. The supportive audience creates an atmosphere where talking during performances is considered disrespectful a rarity in bar settings. The event has run continuously since 1993 including during the 2020 pandemic when it moved to Zoom and was livestreamed to YouTube.

Dining and Amenities

Beyond the music Dornan's operates multiple establishments on the property. The Pizza & Pasta Company serves lunch and dinner year-round inside the Spur Bar featuring New York-style pizza and Italian dishes with panoramic mountain views. The seasonal Chuckwagon restaurant operates during summer months serving breakfast lunch and dinner outdoors. The Trading Post grocery store and deli provides fresh produce baked goods camping supplies and gas making it a one-stop shop for park visitors. The renowned Wine Shop offers an extensive selection curated for discerning tastes.

Lodging and Recreation

Dornan's Spur Ranch Cabins offer year-round accommodations with 8 one-bedroom and 4 two-bedroom cabin duplexes. During summer Adventure Sports rents canoes kayaks and mountain bikes while winter offerings include cross-country skis and snowshoes. The property serves as an ideal base for exploring Grand Teton National Park located just 13 miles from downtown Jackson and 5 miles from Jackson Hole Airport.

Community Gathering Place

For nearly three decades Dornan's has served as a community gathering place where locals and visitors alike share their love of music and the outdoors. The venue's commitment to preserving musical traditions while providing modern amenities has made it an essential part of the Jackson Hole cultural landscape. The family ownership ensures a personal touch and dedication to quality that has kept generations of visitors returning year after year.

title: Wort Hotel - Silver Dollar Bar
venue_description:
Historic Jackson Hole Landmark

The Wort Hotel opened in 1941 when brothers John and Jess Wort transformed their livery stable into what would become Jackson Hole's premier downtown hotel. Located just steps from Town Square the historic property has welcomed everyone from presidents and celebrities to cowboys and everyday travelers for over 80 years. The hotel embodies Western elegance with 55 thoughtfully decorated guest rooms and suites featuring leather furnishings hand-carved wooden bed frames and authentic Western artwork.

The Famous Silver Dollar Bar

The Silver Dollar Bar opened in 1950 and instantly became a Jackson Hole institution. Its most distinctive feature is the 65-foot serpentine bar top inlaid with 2032 uncirculated 1921 Morgan Silver Dollars from the Denver mint. In its early days the bar was a hotspot for drinking socializing and even gambling. The bar's Western decor includes taxidermy displays vintage photographs and an atmosphere that transports patrons to the Wild West while providing modern comforts.

Musical Tradition and Entertainment

The adjacent Silver Dollar Showroom serves as Jackson's premier downtown music venue. Bluegrass Tuesdays featuring the band One Ton Pig has been a beloved tradition for over 15 years with the band playing year-round to packed houses of dancers and music lovers. One Ton Pig was named Best Band in the 2025 Best of Jackson Hole contest. The showroom also hosts live music Thursday Friday and Saturday evenings featuring local regional and national acts across genres from country and folk to rock and bluegrass.

Winter Home of the Hootenanny

Since October 2021 the Silver Dollar Bar has served as the winter home for the legendary Jackson Hole Hootenanny. When Dornan's outdoor venue closes for the season the open mic tradition continues downtown every Monday evening from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM. This partnership ensures the nearly 30-year-old acoustic music tradition runs year-round providing a platform for local and visiting musicians to share two-song sets with an appreciative audience.

Dining Excellence

The Silver Dollar Grill offers upscale Western dining with a menu featuring game and regional fare alongside classic dishes. Open for breakfast lunch and dinner the restaurant has maintained its signature Corn Chowder on the menu continuously since 1985. The family-friendly atmosphere features custom black walnut tables inlaid with silver dollars original Western artwork and even a roulette wheel dating back to Jackson's gambling days. The restaurant boasts an award-winning wine list and cocktail program.

Community Cornerstone

Meet me at the Wort has been a common refrain in Jackson for decades. The hotel and bar have served as an informal assembly point for the town's movers and shakers civic groups the Cattlemen's Association political organizations the chamber of commerce and rodeo clubs. This gathering place tradition continues today with locals and visitors alike meeting at the Wort for business pleasure and musical entertainment. The venue's commitment to live music and preserving Jackson Hole's cultural heritage while providing exceptional hospitality has made it an enduring symbol of the community's spirit.

title: The Virginian Saloon
venue_description:
A Jackson Hole Institution Since 1965

The Virginian Saloon is part of the historic Virginian Lodge which has been welcoming guests to Jackson Hole since 1965. Located on West Broadway within walking distance of downtown Jackson the venue blends rustic Western charm with modern amenities. The saloon features reclaimed wood stone accents vintage decor and an atmosphere that captures the spirit of Wyoming while providing contemporary comforts.

Weekly Open Mic and Jam Sessions

Every Tuesday night the Virginian hosts Open Mic Sessions that take the traditional format to the next level by merging it with jam philosophy. Performers can choose to play solo with a full band or any combination creating a flexible and supportive environment. The night begins with open mic performances and evolves into a community jam session where musicians join together. All types of performances are encouraged including musicians poets comedians and performers of all kinds and abilities. Both participants and audience members are welcomed to enjoy the evening.

Diverse Entertainment Options

Beyond the Tuesday open mic the Virginian offers a wide range of entertainment throughout the week. Industry Nights on Mondays feature bingo trivia rotating themes and surprise events with late-night happy hour starting at 8:30 PM. The venue regularly hosts live music from regional and national bands karaoke sessions and special themed events. Multiple flatscreen TVs make it a popular destination for sports enthusiasts looking to catch their favorite teams.

Food and Drink

The Virginian Saloon partners with Billy's Burgers to offer tasty diner-style fare and pub favorites. The menu features classic American food including juicy burgers crispy wings and flavorful appetizers at reasonable prices. The full bar serves local craft beers creative cocktails and fine wines. Happy hour runs from 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM daily with the saloon open from 4:00 PM until late every night.

Community Hub

The Virginian has established itself as an important venue for Jackson Hole's emerging artists and music community. The supportive atmosphere and accessible format make it an ideal launching pad for up-and-coming performers while also attracting established musicians passing through the valley. The saloon's commitment to providing affordable entertainment in a welcoming Western atmosphere has made it a beloved gathering place for locals and visitors seeking an authentic Jackson Hole experience.

title: Pinky G's Pizzeria
venue_description:
Jackson Hole's Favorite Pizza Spot

Pinky G's Pizzeria opened in 2011 in the Pink Garter Plaza just off Jackson's Town Square. Owner Tom Fay created a laid-back space that isn't pretentious where friends and families can enjoy New York-style pizza in a casual atmosphere. The venue takes its name from its location below the Pink Garter Theatre and features a brick interior reminiscent of a New York City pizzeria with eight flatscreen TVs and a small stage for live performances.

Featured on Food Network

Pinky G's has been featured twice on Guy Fieri's Diners Drive-Ins and Dives on Food Network in 2014 and 2024 showcasing their hand-tossed pizzas and unique creations. The most popular pie is the Abe Froman which has become a local legend. Since opening Pinky G's has been voted Jackson Hole's favorite pizzeria annually by locals. USA Today called it one of the most reasonably priced restaurants in Wyoming's highest rent town making it accessible in an expensive resort community.

All-Ages Open Mic Nights

Every Monday from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM Pinky G's hosts an all-ages open mic night perfect for emerging artists and established performers alike. The early evening timeslot makes it especially accessible for younger musicians who often don't have opportunities to perform at traditional bar venues. Musicians are limited to three songs per performance to ensure everyone gets a turn though repeats are welcome if time allows. The pizzeria keeps several guitars on hand for performers who are traveling through or don't have their own instruments.

Supporting Local Musicians

Each performer who takes the stage receives a free tallboy beer or free slice of pizza as an incentive to participate. The event was originally created by musician David Cattani to provide a supportive comfortable environment for up-and-coming artists. The open mic nights are now hosted by Pinky G's staff and continue to serve as an important platform for the local music community. Beyond Monday open mics the venue hosts live music performances throughout the week featuring favorite Jackson Hole musicians.

Menu and Hours

Pinky G's serves whole pies and pizza by the slice along with calzones chicken tenders mozzarella sticks and salads. The full bar offers craft beers wine and cocktails. The restaurant is open Sunday through Wednesday from 11:00 AM to 9:00 PM and Thursday through Saturday from 11:00 AM to 10:00 PM making it a popular late-night destination. Lunch specials make it a favorite midday stop for locals and visitors exploring Town Square.

Community Gathering Place

Pinky G's prides itself on being a pizzeria that has something for everyone. The combination of quality affordable food a welcoming atmosphere and commitment to live music has made it more than just a restaurant it's become a community hub where locals gather and visitors feel at home. The venue's support for local artists and dedication to providing family-friendly entertainment ensures it remains an essential part of Jackson's cultural landscape.

title: Stagecoach Bar
venue_description:
A Wyoming Institution Since 1942

The Stagecoach Bar has been a cornerstone of the Jackson Hole community since 1942 making it one of the oldest continuously operating establishments in the area. Located in Wilson Wyoming at the base of Teton Pass about 20 minutes from downtown Jackson the venue is affectionately known as The Coach by locals. The bar embodies authentic Wyoming character with its long wooden bar pool tables rustic decor and unpretentious atmosphere that welcomes everyone from cowboys to tourists.

Sunday Church - A 40-Year Tradition

Sunday nights at the Stagecoach have become legendary thanks to the world-famous Stagecoach Band which has performed every Sunday from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM for over 40 years. The band has played more than 2500 nights during their tenure making it one of the longest-running weekly performances in the country. Going to church on Sunday evening is local slang for heading to the Stagecoach to dance to live country and Western swing music. The five-member band draws packed crowds that fill the large dance floor with dancers of all skill levels from seasoned two-steppers to enthusiastic beginners.

Disco Night and Live Music

Thursday nights feature Disco Night during both winter and summer seasons with a DJ spinning classic hits from the 70s and 80s. The dance floor heats up as patrons groove to nostalgic tunes in a lively atmosphere. Friday and Saturday nights often host one-off shows featuring touring regional and national acts across various genres. The venue's commitment to live music seven nights a week has made it an essential stop for music lovers visiting Jackson Hole.

Food and Amenities

The Stagecoach Grill serves affordable Mexican food burgers and pub fare with locals raving about the quality and prices. During summer months guests can enjoy the outdoor deck with picnic tables and beach volleyball adding to the casual fun atmosphere. The bar offers eight beers on tap and a full liquor selection. Pool and darts provide additional entertainment and the venue includes a full-service liquor store with a convenient drive-up window.

Cultural Landmark

The Stagecoach Bar represents a vanishing slice of Americana an authentic dive bar that has resisted the trend toward trendy upscale establishments. Its survival in an increasingly expensive resort town speaks to its importance as a community gathering place. The venue's commitment to affordable prices live music and maintaining its genuine Western character has made it beloved by locals and a must-visit destination for visitors seeking an authentic Wyoming experience. The 70-year-old institution continues to be where locals go and where tourists are told they absolutely must stop during their Jackson Hole visit.

title: Million Dollar Cowboy Bar
venue_description:
A Wyoming Landmark Since 1937

The Million Dollar Cowboy Bar is an iconic music venue and watering hole located on Town Square in the heart of Jackson Wyoming. True to its name this is no ordinary honkytonk it's a historic landmark that has been entertaining locals and visitors since 1937. The bar's distinctive features include saddle barstools Western artwork taxidermy and an atmosphere steeped in cowboy culture and Wyoming heritage.

Live Music Seven Days a Week

The Million Dollar Cowboy Bar is internationally famous for its live entertainment and Western dancing. The venue hosts live music every day of the week featuring everything from local bands to nationally touring acts. Through the decades some of country music's finest entertainers have graced its historic stage including legends like Waylon Jennings Willie Nelson Glen Campbell and Tanya Tucker in the 70s and 80s. In recent years the tradition has continued with performances by Hank Williams Jr. Kevin Costner Clint Black Sara Evans Midland Riley Green and many others.

Million Dollar Music Fest

Each year the bar presents the Million Dollar Music Fest a free outdoor concert held on Town Square during Old West Days in late May. The 2025 festival featured headliners Midland John Michael Montgomery and Tenille Townes drawing thousands to celebrate Jackson's Western heritage. The event includes a kick-off show at the Cowboy Bar featuring emerging artists and an after-party with favorite performers continuing late into the night.

Cowgirls at the Cowboy

The venue hosts Cowgirls at the Cowboy the nation's only all-female country music festival each October. Curated by Nashville artist Jenny Tolman the three-night festival celebrates women in country music with performances from standout artists. The 2025 edition featured headliner Ella Langley fresh off winning five Academy of Country Music Awards along with songwriter showcases and emerging artist nights.

Atmosphere and Experience

The bar maintains its commitment to offering both ticketed headline shows and regular nightly entertainment where locals and travelers can experience authentic Jackson Hole nightlife. Whether dancing to a touring act or enjoying the house band the Million Dollar Cowboy Bar provides an unforgettable Western experience. The venue's blend of history live music and cowboy culture makes it essential to any Jackson Hole visit and a gathering place where countless celebrities presidents and people from all walks of life have enjoyed the excitement for which this iconic bar is known.
